title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
abstract: arXiv:2610.29139v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitf

translated_title: 使用陷阱预期世界模型引导黑盒大语言模型智能体
translated_abstract: 前沿的黑盒大语言模型智能体擅长长程推理和精确的动作生成。然而，在执行特定智能体任务时，它们并没有内化关于该特定环境如何演变的认识。世界模型提供了一种天然的解决方案，通过预见环境对智能体即将采取的行动的响应，为智能体提供环境特定的知识。先前面向LLM智能体的世界模型主要在每个步骤预测下一个观测，这既成本高昂又往往缺乏信息量，因为单个观测所能提供的任务相关指导有限，而且并非每个步骤都需要前瞻性预测。这引出一个关键问题：对于智能体任务，世界模型应该预测什么，以及何时应该被调用？我们的初步研究表明，当世界模型在有限的多步未来内预期陷阱时，其指导最为有用。受此启发，我们引入了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种“陷阱预期世界模型”，通过在有限的多步未来内预判潜在陷阱（而非逐步预测下一个观测），以更高效、更具指导性的方式引导黑盒大语言模型智能体完成智能体任务。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Pitfall Anticipation World Model that steers black-box LLM agents by anticipating pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future, rather than making costly and often uninformative step-by-step next-observation predictions.
